evidence: Plan step 4: 'run the existing agentic completion-verifier scoped to only the ABSTAINed ACs (harness-level criteria subsetting; read-only --source local, never signs).'
src/rebar/llm/completion.py:120 `verify_completion(ticket_id, *, graph, ref, source, fetch, repo_root, config, runner)` — no criteria-subset parameter.

findings.finding: Step 4 asserts 'harness-level criteria subsetting' to run the existing completion-verifier 'scoped to only the ABSTAINed ACs,' but no such subsetting seam exists on the integration and the plan's own constraints forbid the obvious workarounds.
findings.location: Protocol step 4 / AC line 'run the existing agentic completion-verifier scoped to only the ABSTAINed ACs'
scenarios: Author reaches step 4 and finds no flag/param to limit the verifier to abstained ACs; must either patch src/rebar (violates AC-1), write a mutated ticket (violates AC-5), or drive the internal `verify_completion(...)` on a synthetic in-ticket object — none of which the plan specifies.

If the fallback silently verifies ALL ACs instead of only abstained ones, the step-4 cost/step/token metric (the experiment's core deliverable) no longer measures 'narrowed' agentic work and the coverage-savings conclusion is invalid.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 4, replace 'harness-level criteria subsetting' with the exact seam: from the throwaway harness, build an in-memory ticket dict whose ACs are only the ABSTAINed ones and pass it to `rebar.llm.completion.verify_completion(...)` (in-process, `source='local'`, no sign, no store write), OR run the unmodified verifier over the whole ticket and post-filter its findings to the abstained ACs for the cost comparison — and state which.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the filter-pass fallback: any emission that is not a clean PASS (a FAIL, a malformed/unparseable reply, or an AC with no verdict) is coerced to ABSTAIN and routed to the step-4 agentic verifier, so no AC can be dropped or rejected by the filter.
evidence: Step 3: 'ONE LLM call, no tools ... emit per AC either PASS(with citations) or ABSTAIN. The contract forbids FAIL.'
Step 4 routes only 'the ABSTAINed ACs' to the agentic verifier, so any AC without a clean PASS/ABSTAIN verdict has no defined destination.

Why: 'false-positive rejection is impossible by construction' — this holds only if every non-PASS emission (including a forbidden FAIL or malformed/absent verdict) is coerced to ABSTAIN and routed to the fallback; that coercion rule is absent.
ABSENCE: no sentence specifies malformed-reply handling, per-AC verdict-parse failure, or FAIL-emitted-despite-ban handling.
findings.finding: The filter pass (single tool-less LLM call) has no specified fallback for a failed or contract-violating emission: what the harness does when the call emits a FAIL (which the contract forbids but a model may still produce), returns a malformed/unparseable reply, or omits a verdict for one or more ACs is never stated.
findings.location: Protocol step 3 (Filter pass) and step 4 (Fallback); Why paragraph ('false-positive rejection is impossible by construction')
scenarios: The model emits FAIL for an AC despite the forbidding instruction; without a coercion rule the harness could record a rejection, contradicting the 'impossible by construction' claim.
The single call returns unparseable JSON or drops verdicts for a subset of ACs; those ACs are neither PASSed nor routed to step 4, silently dropping them from coverage and false-PASS accounting.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 3: 'Parse the single reply per AC. Any AC not emitting a well-formed PASS-with-citations — including a FAIL (contract violation), a malformed/unparseable verdict, or an omitted AC — is treated as ABSTAIN and forwarded to step 4. Record contract violations in the metrics table as a separate count.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Measure false-PASS at the SYSTEM level (filter PASS + fallback PASS combined) on every adversarial unmet AC, not only at the filter step, and report both.
evidence: Step 5: 'false-PASS count on adversarial unmet ACs (MUST be 0 for the design to survive)' — attributed to step 3 (the filter)
Step 4 runs the agentic verifier on ABSTAINed ACs; if the filter correctly ABSTAINs on an adversarial-unmet AC, the fallback can still wrongly PASS it
Verdict AC asks whether filter+fallback beats pure-agentic 'WITHOUT any false PASS' — a system-level property
findings.finding: The false-PASS metric is scoped only to the filter (step 3), but the end-to-end system can still emit a false PASS via the agentic FALLBACK; the verdict AC's safety claim ('WITHOUT any false PASS') is therefore not fully measured.
scenarios: Filter ABSTAINs on an edited (unmet) AC (correct, no filter false-PASS), then the scoped agentic verifier PASSes it → a real system false-PASS that the step-3 metric does not count
findings.suggested_fix: In step 5 split false-PASS into 'filter false-PASS' and 'fallback false-PASS', and require the SYSTEM total (either path passing an adversarial-unmet AC) to be 0 for the design to survive.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that positive-corpus ground truth is close-gate-derived (a proxy), and rely on the hand-edited adversarial ACs (independently known unmet) as the authoritative false-PASS oracle; optionally spot-check a sample of positive ACs by hand.

findings.finding: Ground truth for the real (non-adversarial) tickets is defined as 'all ACs met because they passed the close gate' — a proxy that inherits any false-passes of the existing verifier this work exists to replace, so a filter false-PASS on a truly-unmet AC would be scored as correct.

scenarios: A closed ticket that the existing verifier false-passed is used as a 'all ACs met' positive; the new filter also PASSes it → recorded as a correct PASS, masking a false PASS on the positive corpus

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Why section, situate the filter+fallback design against established LLM-cascade prior art (FrugalGPT, AutoMix) and abstention/selective-prediction work, and state explicitly what is novel here (e.g. per-criterion PASS/ABSTAIN over natural-language ACs with an evidence prepack) vs what is standard cascading.
evidence: Plan 'Why': 'use the single pass as a FILTER that may only PASS or ABSTAIN per criterion (never reject), then run the existing agentic verifier scoped to the remaining criteria'; 'false-positive rejection is impossible by construction'
Plan grounds the design only in internal 'Experience says' and the operator counter-proposal; no external prior art cited anywhere in the plan or parent ticket b4be-0ed8-22cb-4b01

Retrieved: FrugalGPT (emergentmind.com/topics/frugalgpt) and AutoMix (arxiv.org/pdf/2310.12963) — LLM cascades where a cheap model answers, a verifier/scorer evaluates, and escalation to a stronger model happens only when the scorer signals insufficiency

Retrieved: 'Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models' (arxiv.org/html/2407.18418) and confidence-based / selective-prediction abstention literature — the ABSTAIN mechanism the filter relies on

Retrieved: a three-way claim-disposition design discussion (admit/refute/abstain) noting that a one-sided 'refute-or-abstain' pass amplifies the model's dominant error direction — directly relevant to the plan's choice of PASS-only one-sidedness to avoid false rejection
findings.finding: The plan introduces a filter+fallback verification architecture (single PASS/ABSTAIN pass, then scoped agentic verification of ABSTAINed criteria) and asserts a structural novelty ('false-positive rejection is impossible by construction'; 'narrowing agentic work, not eliminating it') without any consideration of established prior art. This pattern is a well-documented LLM cascade (FrugalGPT: cheap model + post-query scorer that escalates only on low confidence; AutoMix: self-verify then route to a larger model), i.e. ABSTAIN == escalate. There is also directly relevant prior art on the one-sided-disposition design choice the plan's thesis depends on. The plan should situate its design against, and justify novelty vs, this literature.
findings.location: Why section + Protocol steps 3-4 (filter pass / fallback)
scenarios: Reviewers/operator deciding go/no-go on productizing cannot tell whether the design repackages FrugalGPT/AutoMix cascades or genuinely differs

Metrics chosen for the PoC (coverage, false-PASS, cost delta) may miss lessons already known from cascade literature about cascade collapse (everything escalating) and calibration-driven abstention quality
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art' subsection to Why: note that ABSTAIN==escalate makes this a two-stage LLM cascade in the FrugalGPT/AutoMix family, cite the abstention/selective-prediction literature for the ABSTAIN contract, and justify the genuinely novel element (deterministic per-AC evidence prepack + PASS-only filter over prose ACs). Fold known cascade risks (cascade collapse = universal escalation; calibration of abstention) into the metrics/failure-modes the PoC will measure.
